title: Fixed ei ole with plural owners
summary: Use fixed ei ole with meillä, teillä, and heillä when possession is denied.
objectives: Use fixed ei ole with meillä, teillä, and heillä when possession is denied.
Apply the pattern using the supporting forms shown.

sections.title: How the pattern works
paragraphs: Use fixed ei ole with meillä, teillä, and heillä when possession is denied.
Meillä ei ole palloa means “We do not have a ball”. Several owners still use ei ole; do not change it to emme ole.
keyPoints: Use fixed ei ole with meillä, teillä, and heillä when possession is denied.

examples.english: We do not have a car.
steps: meillä means “we as the owner”.
With several owners, meillä still takes ei ole, not emme ole.
The complete noun form autoa (“a car”) is shown here; its formation is taught in the “Regular negative noun forms with plural owners” lesson.

examples.english: You do not have a game.
steps: teillä means “you as the owner” for a group.
Teillä still takes ei ole, not ette ole, even though the owner is a group.
The complete noun form peliä (“a game”) is shown here; its formation is taught in the “Regular negative noun forms with plural owners” lesson.

examples.english: They do not have a pen.
steps: heillä means “they as the owner”.
Heillä still takes ei ole, not eivät ole. Only the owner phrase has changed.
The complete noun form kynää (“a pen”) is shown here; its formation is taught in the “Regular negative noun forms with plural owners” lesson.

examples.english: We do not have a pillow.
steps: meillä means “we as the owner”.
The front vowels in the noun affect its noun ending, not fixed ei ole.
The complete noun form tyynyä (“a pillow”) is shown here; its formation is taught in the “Regular negative noun forms with plural owners” lesson.

examples.english: You do not have a book.
steps: teillä identifies the plural owner in this fixed ei ole with plural owners pattern.
Use owner + ei ole; possession keeps the verb pattern fixed.
kirjaa (“a book”) is the complete regular singular partitive: kirja + -a.

examples.english: You do not have a cat.
steps: teillä identifies the plural owner in this fixed ei ole with plural owners pattern.
Use owner + ei ole; possession keeps the verb pattern fixed.
kissaa (“a cat”) is the complete regular singular partitive: kissa + -a.

examples.english: They do not have a dog.
steps: heillä identifies the plural owner in this fixed ei ole with plural owners pattern.
Use owner + ei ole; possession keeps the verb pattern fixed.
koiraa (“a dog”) is the complete regular singular partitive: koira + -a.

commonMistakes: Keep both words ei ole: ei alone leaves the negative possession pattern incomplete.
Use meillä ei ole and heillä ei ole, rather than person-conjugated emme ole or eivät ole.
Use the complete noun form shown in these verb questions; the partitive lesson teaches how to form it.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Write “They do not have a ball.” in Finnish. Use heillä (“they as the owner”) and palloa (“a ball”). Frame: “Heillä ___ palloa”.
practiceExercises.explanation: Use fixed ei ole after heillä. The owner phrase does not make ei agree with a subject.

sentenceExplanation.translation: They do not have a ball.
sentenceExplanation.pattern: possessor + fixed ei ole + singular partitive noun

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: he has the learned possession form heillä; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
Possession uses fixed ei with meillä, teillä and heillä; do not change it to emme, ette or eivät.
After ei, olla uses ole. Together ei ole means “do not have” or “does not have” here.
pallo + -a = palloa. This is the singular partitive, the noun form used when possession is denied.

answerDiagnostics.category: Fixed ei ole in possession: predictable form error
answerDiagnostics.explanation: The -lla/-llä phrase is the possessor. In this possession pattern the verb stays fixed, so do not conjugate it to match the owner.
